records.notes: Closes #483, and is the first case to invoke `set-up` at all (the subcommand joined `CONSUMER_SUBCOMMANDS` / `CONTAINER_SUBCOMMANDS` for it). The claim is the SHAPE of the `--include-merged-configuration` block, which had three defects at once: deacon emitted its flat configuration under a snake_case `merged_configuration` key, with the five lifecycle hooks as SINGULAR fields, where the reference emits `mergedConfiguration` carrying the collected plural arrays. Two operations are needed because the merge has two sources that must both land, in order: `op-up` stamps the workspace config into the container's `devcontainer.metadata` label, and `op-set-up` layers a SECOND, differently-worded config on top with `--config`. So `onCreateCommands` must be `["echo base-onCreate", "echo overlay-onCreate"]` — collected, and devcontainer.json-last per the spec's image-metadata Merge Logic. Identical hook text in both sources would have made the collection and the ordering unobservable, which is why the overlay's commands are worded differently rather than repeated. The differential is what pins ORDER (array comparison is positional); the `jsonSubset` assertion is the absolute claim on deacon's side, so a run where BOTH CLIs stopped collecting could not pass. `chan-stdout` is deliberately NOT declared: both sides emit the same document with different key ORDER, which is a difference in serialization rather than in behavior and is exactly what the structured channel exists to see past. Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on this fixture; the two sides' `mergedConfiguration` agree on every key after normalization, with the three synthesized empties (`remoteEnv`, `containerEnv`, `portsAttributes`) elided on both sides by the `drop_absent_optional` rule — the standing `bhv-readconfig-merged-computed-empties-omitted` characterization, not a tolerance this case declares. Image pinned to alpine:3.19 (V18).

Closes #502, the one difference `case-set-up-merged-configuration-shape` measured on this surface and left without a scenario. The claim is that `--include-configuration` reports what the CALLER SUPPLIED — the `--config` document alone — and not what set-up resolved: `mergedConfiguration` (the sibling case) is where the merge belongs, the same authored-vs-resolved contract #490 and #407 settled elsewhere. The fixture is built so the fold is VISIBLE rather than merely absent: the workspace config authors `remoteUser` and `containerEnv`, which `op-up` stamps into the container's `devcontainer.metadata` label, and the overlay authors NEITHER. deacon folded the label into the block, so both appeared there as though the caller had written them; the reference echoes only the overlay. A `jsonSubset` cannot assert a key's ABSENCE, so those two keys are pinned by the DIFFERENTIAL — the reference is the authority on a spec-silent output surface — while the absolute deacon-side claim is `configFilePath`, which deacon omitted entirely and which no CLI emits by accident. Its `scheme` is `file` rather than the `vscode-fileHost` the same reference uses for `read-configuration`, and that falls out of the existing `config_file_path_value` rule (scheme keyed off whether the caller NAMED the file) rather than being a set-up special case. Also measured on the same oracle and NOT asserted here, because both sides agree and a case should claim what it pins: with no `--config` at all the reference emits `"configuration": {}` — an empty document, no `configFilePath` — and so does deacon. `chan-stdout` is deliberately NOT declared, for the same key-ordering reason as the sibling case. Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on this fixture; the two sides' `configuration` blocks agree on every key after normalization (`path_token` rewrites the per-side temp workspace to `<WORKSPACE>`), and the case declares no tolerance. Image pinned to alpine:3.19.

Closes #510, the one difference `case-set-up-configuration-authored` measured on this surface and left without a scenario. The claim is the SCOPE of variable substitution: `set-up` takes no `--workspace-folder`, so `${localWorkspaceFolder}`, `${localWorkspaceFolderBasename}` and `${devcontainerId}` have no answer and the reference leaves all three LITERAL, while `${localEnv:*}` still resolves. deacon anchored its `SubstitutionContext` at the process cwd and substituted an invented workspace into both. The case observes the two surfaces the defect actually reaches. `chan-structured-output` pins the reported blocks — the same three tokens must survive verbatim in BOTH `configuration` and `mergedConfiguration`, because the two blocks are shaped by different code paths and an earlier fix to one has already left the other behind here (#483/#502). `chan-file-content` pins what set-up RAN, which is the half no assertion on the JSON can see: the overlay's `postCreateCommand` writes the three tokens to a file, and the reference's literal tokens reach the container shell as unset names and expand to empty, so the artifact is `ws=[] base=[] id=[]` — where deacon wrote the cwd, its basename and a computed id into the command string host-side. The artifact is host-visible because the BASE fixture pins `workspaceFolder: /work` with a matching `workspaceMount`, giving the hook a bind-mounted absolute path instead of the per-side random `/workspaces/<basename>`; the hook writes to that absolute path, so the exec cwd (which the two CLIs need not agree on) cannot affect the result. `--container-data-folder` is NOT incidental: `op-up` leaves the reference's lifecycle markers in the default folder and a marked phase does not re-run, so without a fresh folder the hook is silently skipped and the execution channel would pass while proving nothing. The overlay deliberately authors NO `${containerWorkspaceFolder}`: that variable diverges on this surface in a different way (deacon never resolves it in the reported blocks and invents `/` at exec time when unauthored), which is a different defect in kind, filed as #513 — including it would have coupled this case to an unsettled question instead of pinning the three variables it is about. `${localEnv:HOME}` is authored but NOT asserted absolutely, because its value is host-specific; the differential covers it, and it is the control that shows the fix gated the workspace variables rather than the whole pass. `chan-stdout` is deliberately NOT declared, for the same key-ordering reason as the sibling cases. Measured against oracle 0.87.0 on this fixture; the two sides agree on every declared channel after normalization, and the case declares no tolerance. Image pinned to alpine:3.19. One assertion is written in POST-NORMALIZATION vocabulary and must stay that way: the `devcontainer_id_token` rule rewrites the literal `${devcontainerId}` to `<ID>` everywhere in `configuration`/`mergedConfiguration`, so the absolute claim on `PROBE_DEVCONTAINER_ID` is `<ID>`, not the raw token. That rule is also why the DIFFERENTIAL on this key cannot be the thing that pins it — both a literal token and a substituted 12-char hex id normalize into that field's `<ID>` — which is exactly why the case carries the absolute assertion and the execution channel as well. The two `localWorkspaceFolder*` keys are NOT rewritten by any rule, so they are asserted as the raw tokens and are the sharpest claim in the case.
